description: Mira checks nginx and the Pixel Raiders game server on the build server with systemctl, reads their logs with journalctl and /var/log/syslog, and looks at the kernel messages with dmesg.
environment: Each host ran in a Docker container on Docker Desktop (arm64), so the kernel is Docker Desktop's (Linux 7.0.14-linuxkit), not the distribution's.
On the Debian hosts, systemd runs as PID 1, as on a real machine.
The hosts share a network in documentation address ranges (192.0.2.0/24 and 2001:db8:1::/64, gateway 192.0.2.1). A dnsmasq container at 192.0.2.53 answers for tuxpixel.example.
Commands ran in a login shell on an 80-column terminal, with the pagers of systemd and dpkg turned off (SYSTEMD_PAGER=cat, DPKG_PAGER=cat).
Sockets on 127.0.0.11 belong to Docker's built-in DNS service, which every container on such a network has.
nginx is set to start 2 worker processes rather than one per CPU, to keep process listings short.
rsyslog was installed so that /var/log/syslog exists; since Debian 12 it is no longer installed by default, and the systemd journal keeps the logs.
The game server is a stand-in script (see the setup), so its log lines are what that script prints.

setup.command:
cat > /usr/local/bin/pixel-raiders-server <<'LE_EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Stand-in for the Pixel Raiders game server: it reads its settings and stays running.
conf=/etc/pixel-raiders/server.conf
if [ ! -r "$conf" ]; then
  echo "pixel-raiders-server: cannot read $conf" >&2
  exit 1
fi
. "$conf"
echo "Pixel Raiders server 1.1: map $MAP, up to $MAX_PLAYERS players"
while sleep 30; do echo "players online: 0"; done
LE_EOF
chmod 755 /usr/local/bin/pixel-raiders-server

cat > /etc/systemd/system/pixel-raiders-server.service <<'LE_EOF'
[Unit]
Description=Pixel Raiders game server
After=network.target

[Service]
User=pixelraiders
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/pixel-raiders-server

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
LE_EOF
chmod 644 /etc/systemd/system/pixel-raiders-server.service
